hook_text: Put two maps side by side: 1860 and 1913. Count the African kingdoms on each.
clip_script: 1860. Two British colonies on the coast. Two Boer republics inland. And all around them, independent kingdoms: the Zulu, the Pedi, the Swazi, the Basotho, the Xhosa chiefdoms, the Tswana. Then diamonds in 1867. Gold in 1886. Britain wanted the minerals, the land and the workers. 1879: the Zulu and the Pedi are defeated. 1902: the Boer republics are conquered. 1910: four colonies become one Union. Now 1913. One big shape covers the map. Around it, three British protectorates that later became Lesotho, Botswana and Eswatini. Fifty-three years. That is why it is called a turning point.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of southern Africa in 1860 with many labelled pieces, morphing into the 1913 map with one large Union shape and small protectorates around it.
pacing: Fast through the events, pausing on each map.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how to compare historical maps for marks.
